etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English driere, dreyere (“one who dries”), equivalent to dry +‎ -er (agent noun suffix).

definitions.definition: One who, or that which, dries; a desiccative.
A household appliance that removes the water from clothing by accelerating evaporation, usually through heat and a tumbling motion.

quote.citation: 1996, Curriculum Corporation (Australia), From Igloos to Yurts: Years 4-7, page 23:
quote.text: Assist students to design and construct models of hot-air balloons ranging from those using shopping bags and hair dryers, to those using tissue paper and metho burners, depending on the resources available.

definitions.definition: Any other device or facility, household or industrial, designed to remove water or humidity.

quote.citation: 2004 December 17, Evgenii D. Moniushko, From Leningrad to Hungary: Notes of a Red Army Soldier, 1941-1946, Routledge, →ISBN, page 51:
quote.text: At that time, father, brother and I worked as night watchmen at the grain dryer. It was a large and complicated structure built out in the steppe. It consisted of a wooden tower with swinging shelves attached to the inside walls, […]

definitions.definition: A catalyst used to promote the drying of paints and varnishes by oxidative crosslinking.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From dry +‎ -er (comparative suffix).

definitions.definition: (US) comparative form of dry: more dry
